analysis.title: Persist customer email during order save

summary.headline: SaveOrder now passes customerEmail into SaveOrderDB so the orders table can persist it.
items: SaveOrderDBInput gained a new string field: customerEmail.
SaveOrder flow added one MAPCOPY from OrderDocument/order/customerEmail to SaveOrderDBInput/customerEmail.
SaveOrderDB SQL now inserts customer_email and expects one additional bind parameter.
No new service invocation was introduced; the execution path is unchanged.

aiExplanation.summary: SaveOrder now forwards customerEmail into SaveOrderDB to persist customer contact data into the orders table. The scope is localized to the persistence contract and input mapping with no alterations to upstream scheduler or orchestration flows.

sections.What Changed: SaveOrderDBInput gained a new string field customerEmail. SaveOrder flow added a MAPCOPY step connecting OrderDocument/order/customerEmail to SaveOrderDBInput/customerEmail. The SQL fixture was updated to insert customer_email with six parameter placeholders instead of five.
sections.Impact Path: Changes originate in the SaveOrder flow mapping and propagate downstream to SaveOrderDB and the orders database table. Direct caller OrderProcessing and the scheduled trigger remain unimpacted in signature and orchestration flow.
sections.Risk Analysis: Assessed at Medium risk (score 64). The primary drivers are the modified adapter input contract and database insert parameter alignment. The risk remains contained because no transaction orchestration or business validation rules were altered.
sections.Testing Rationale: Regression testing focuses on verifying database insertion with customerEmail present and absent, confirming parameter ordering in the SQL statement, and ensuring existing order fields remain unaffected.
